programme.desc: Nathan, who works 800 feet underground in a limestone mine, tells the story of the season's first big buck — a 190-inch Kentucky giant taken on just 147 acres.

programme.desc: Spice lovers rejoice as daring heat and bold seasonings transform everyday dishes into fiery, unforgettable griddle creations.

programme.title: Big Buck Blue Print
programme.desc: 8 year old Brantly takes a buck of a lifetime!

programme.title: Redemption Season: A DIY Public Land Elk Hunt
programme.desc: Eastmans' videographer Lindsay steps in front of the camera with an October public-land elk tag. Warm weather, fog and a high snow line keep the post-rut bulls in the timber, so she glasses new country solo off an onX waypoint, hunting for one more chance before the season runs out.

programme.title: Waterfowl Hunting: The Ultimate Mixed Bag Morning
programme.desc: The Wingmen crew and family hit a river goose spot on a warm, windy December morning. With mild weather keeping the birds scarce, it turns into a slow-burn hunt, as widgeon, a mallard and a rare gadwall hen fall over the decoys. Along the way, they explain how to tell a mature widgeon hen from a juvenile by its wing feathers.

programme.title: Would You Hunt with the 22 Creedmoor? Speed Test & Hornady Review
programme.desc: Can a .22-caliber rifle reach 1,500 yards? Todd Helms puts Hornady's 22 Creedmoor to the test with four loads: Precision Hunter, Match, V-Match and Superformance CX. He shoots groups and clocks velocities over the chronograph, and shares the Wyoming mule deer he took with the 80-grain ELD-X.

programme.title: Grit Pays Off! DIY Elk Bow Hunt with Brian Barney
programme.desc: Twelve days into a tough September elk season, Brian Barney and buddy Dylan Ness pack a lightweight spike camp into public-land bowls and glass for a mature six-point. With an hour of light left, they ditch their packs, sprint to the next ridge and use the terrain to stalk into bow range. Then comes the hard part: breaking down the bull and getting the meat off the mountain on no sleep.

programme.title: 3-Man Limit! River Duck Hunt with Wingmen
programme.desc: Crawl in the blind for a late-season waterfowl hunt on the river with the Wingmen crew. Todd Helms is joined by good friends Josh and Greg for some fellowship, and hopefully decoying a few ducks. Weather has been mild and the local birds are stale, but the guys manage to fill out a three-man limit on greenheads with some bonus geese in the mix.

programme.title: Sig Sauer Image Stabilizing Binoculars
programme.desc: Mike Eastman reviews Sig Sauer's Zulu6 HDX image-stabilizing binoculars. He shows how stabilization takes the shake out of glassing in the wind, why the 20-power model can replace a spotting scope in your pack, and how the upgraded HDX glass performs in low light.

programme.title: Public Land Beast! Bow Hunting Big Bulls with Brian Barney
programme.desc: Join Eastmans' Elevated podcast host Brian Barney on this Beyond the Grid episode to bow hunt elk in the rugged backcountry in pursuit of arrowing a bugling bull! This DIY bow hunt is packed with navigating new valleys, winter weather, and Brian's signature spot-and-stalk tactics. From glassing ridges at first light to heart-pounding moments with screaming bulls, this is elk hunting in the raw.

programme.title: Whitetail Properties
programme.desc: Iowa Land Specialist Ben Harshyne chases an awesome buck on his Iowa farm with bow in hand. Followed up by Missouri Land Specialist Jeff Propst chasing a buck during the firearm season.

programme.desc: Archie is gung-ho to want to spread some Christmas cheer, annoying his more cynical friends.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: In the two decades since the state’s tattooing ban was lifted the industry has blossomed in Massachusetts, and tonight we explore this popular form of self-expression. We meet a set of identical twins in Salem who are in the tattoo business together, and a local body art professional who specializes in helping patients who have undergone mastectomy. We also meet artists who specialize in temporary tattoos. And we connect with local pros who specialize in tattoo removal – helping those who regret early choices or see them as a barrier to employment.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: we meet families confronting health challenges – and researchers here in Boston who are determined to cure rare diseases. Erika Tarantal reconnects with a girl with a rare skin disorder who has inspired an entire fundraising movement. We visit Brigham and Women’s Hospital, the only hospital in the country offering screening for Duchenne muscular dystrophy for every newborn.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: New England has no shortage of places to connect (and share) the flavors of home – wherever “home” might be. We find haggis (and Scotch) on the menu at Scottish favorite The Haven in Jamaica Plain, and treasures from the Old Sod at Galway Girl in Duxbury.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Forget the jingle bells and candy canes – New Englanders have some unusual holiday habits!

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: In Vermont’s Deerfield Valley, Shayna Seymour visits Mount Snow and meets the Massachusetts couple who have revived The Hermitage, a shuttered inn transformed into a luxury winter destination. Next door in New Hampshire’s White Mountains, Anthony Everett visits the charming Mountain View Grand Resort in Whitefield, N.H. for winter activities (and gets a lesson in high-performance driving nearby). And if your winter travels lean more toward cities Erika Tarantal hits Providence, R.I., where she checks out the art scene, shops at Greek restaurant and market Yolenis, tours a historic hotel, and even takes a blacksmithing class.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: If winter has you chilled to the bone, we have ideas to warm you up! Erika Tarantal is “skinning” up Black Mountain in Jackson, N.H., then warming up at the Villa Hygge Hotel in North Conway, where she introduces us to the cozy Scandinavian concept of “hygge.” Shayna Seymour heads to Vermont’s Mad River Valley, where diners at the original American Flatbread can dine fireside in their own private cabins. And Nicole Estaphan dines in an igloo in Portland, Maine, and visits a hotel in nearby Cape Elizabeth, where the stories of dog rescues will warm the heart.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Chronicle's award-winning team brings you the stories of New England.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Think lobsters are pricey? They’ve got nothing on “glass eels,” now a beyond-booming industry on the coast of Maine. We visit Ellsworth, where at today’s price of $2,200 a pound, there’s heavy competition to net the tiny, wriggling baby eels for export to Asia. We meet some of the lucky few licensed in the glass eel trade, including the so-called “godfather” of the industry, as well as ordinary Mainers whose fortunes have changed thanks to a coveted license. And we talk to Maine law enforcement about the early days of the eel trade, a wild-west scene replete with guns, cash – and eels.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: There’s just something about the holiday season that kicks the sweet tooth into overdrive. We stop by family-owned shops Hilliard’s in North Easton to spin up homemade candy canes and Winfrey’s on the North Shore where fudge is the main event. At other sweet stops we dig into gooey cinnamon rolls, ghost pepper caramels, peppermint bark (both Christmas and Hanukkah varieties) and get in on the “cocoa bomb” craze. And for a break from the sweet routine we sample specialty roasted nuts at Cacao in Newton.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: chronicle 101226.mp4Pull up a chair! There's always room for one more. We visit a church where a weekly community supper has served more than 65,000 meals; join strangers who become friends through Boston's growing supper club scene; and discover neighborhood diners where regulars gather as much for conversation, as comfort food. Then, step inside an intimate Thai supper club where every meal is shared around the chef’s own dining table. Whether in a church hall, restaurant, or family home, these stories celebrate the power of food to bring people together.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: With three Grammy awards to her name and millions of records sold with The Pointer Sisters, what is Ruth Pointer doing living in a tiny town in central Mass.? Tonight we visit this super septuagenarian at her home (yes, she’s still performing), and meet others who are also shining bright in their golden years. Nicole Estaphan meets the Pom-tastics cheerleading squad, who practice at a local senior center.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Boston culinary icon Lydia Shire is still cooking, still creating – and still inspiring! Tonight she takes us from Chinatown to Cambridge, exploring the dishes and traditions that fuel her imagination—from roast duck to homemade lemongrass oil.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: summer We sample banana soda, spiked blue slushes, and other summer flavors to wet the whistle. Ted Reinstein meets a veteran who retired from the military and opened a candy and ice cream shop, where you have to see the “king shakes” to believe them. In Medfield, we sample a few cold ones at Seventh Wave Brewing, whose owner went from a career selling books to brewing beer and making pizza. We visit Downeast Cider, where it’s not just about the apples; try strawberry, guava and more. And at Harvest in Harvard Square, the head of the cocktail program talks summer trends.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Experience the summer scene in Boston from parks, restaurants and outdoor workout classes, find new acitivies in Boston.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Love true crime? Erika Tarantal talks to the author of Helltown, the story of a serial killer that captivated Cape Cod in the turbulent 1960s. If summer travel is more your style, Erika joins a local travel writer to hit up favorite spots from a new guide to visiting the Cape. Closer to Boston, we meet the owner of a book shop who began selling books from a pushcart before opening her store. Finally, we meet an author whose historical novel highlights immigrant stories from the town of Milford.

programme.desc: Grandmama (Blossom Rock) is hauled off to jail for setting up a fortune-telling booth in the Addamses' living room. Gomez (John Astin) volunteers to act as attorney, and the court session becomes a shambles.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Gomez (John Astin) loses his memory after hitting his head; he fails to recognize Morticia (Carolyn Jones) and says the house looks like a condemned museum. The Addamses take turns hitting Gomez on the head trying to help him regain his memory.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Thing disappears from his box. Failing to find a single trace of Thing, Gomez (John Astin) conducts an investigation--with all members of the household under suspicion. Also starring Carolyn Jones, Jackie Coogan, and Ted Cassidy.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Uncle Fester applies for a job as an insurance salesman with the same company which is threatening to cancel the Addamses' policy (because Fester keeps blowing things up). Fester convinces the company interviewer that he is qualified for the job.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Lurch becomes inconsolable when Gomez donates the family antique harpsichord to a collector. Gomez and Morticia offer Lurch a balalaika and a set of drums. When this proves unsatisfactory, Gomez and Fester decide to build a new harpsichord.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: When Morticia hears the stock market has crashed, she assumes that Gomez has been financially wiped out and rallies the family to help make money. Morticia gives lessons, Lurch and Fester run an escort service, and the kids run a poison drink stand.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.sub-title: The Addams Family And The Spaceman
programme.desc: While enjoying a moonlight picnic and snail hunt, the Addams Family is mistaken for Martians by uniformed investigators from Mysterious Space Objects Headquarters. In turn, Gomez (John Astin) and the clan regard their inquisitors with suspicion.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: An organ grinder's fugitive monkey leads Fester to believe that he has turned Pugsley into a monkey. Morticia and Gomez treat the monkey as though he were their son, welcoming him to the dinner table and giving him Pugsley's chores.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Morticia's favorite charity is having an auction--so Morticia persuades her family to part with things to sell. Donations include Wednesday's headless doll, the old flogging table, a stuffed vulture and Uncle Fester's dynamite.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: The Addams Family ignores notices that their house is to be condemned to make way for a freeway. When sudden explosions cannot be traced to any member of the family but, instead, to city workmen, Gomez is forced to consider moving the house.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Uncle Fester's pen pal, Madelyn, is coming to visit. Fester panics, as he has described himself as handsome, heroic and romantic. Gomez and Morticia agree that all Fester needs is a toupee and they help him make several styles.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.sub-title: Cousin Itt And The Vocational Counselor
programme.desc: Morticia and Gomez are worried about Cousin Itt because he spends his days sleeping and dreaming in his tiny room. They decide that Itt would make an excellent marriage counselor, and pretend to be a couple with a failing marriage.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: A recording company's platter of Lurch's gravelly voice brings a screaming mob of teenage fans to the Addams house. To calm the crowd, Lurch seats himself at the harpsichord and rewards his fans with a song to end all songs.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Taken in by a psychologist's pronouncement that the only happily married couples are those who fight members of the Addams household devise schemes to start a battle between Gomez (John Astin) and Morticia (Carolyn Jones).

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Gomez decides to bolster Cousin Itt's failing ego by making him the star of a production aimed as a birthday surprise for Wednesday. He hires the great director, Eric von Bissell, who gives Itt elocution lessons, causing a Hollywood star complex.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: While Morticia and Gomez are celebrating their 13th wedding anniversary, she tells Wednesday and Pugsley a bedtime story of how she and Gomez first met. In this episode, Carolyn Jones plays Morticia, Morticia as a 22-year-old, and sister Ophelia.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Wednesday and Pugsley refuse to go to bed until they hear the rest of the courtship story. Morticia resumes the tale via flashback, including the ceremony beginning with Ophelia Frump, Morticia's balmy sister, as the bride.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Romance seems close for Thing, the Addams right-hand-in-a-box, when Gomez's aunt arrives for a visit accompanied by Lady Fingers, her handmaiden. Thing enjoys the visit most because it gives him a chance to hold hands with one of his own kind.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Morticia and Gomez visit Mayor Henson to complain that their property tax is ridiculously low. After the Mayor proves his incompetence by offering a refund, Gomez is persuaded to become a candidate for the office.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: During a welcome home party for Cousin Itt, Morticia notices that the diminutive guest of honor seems to be losing his hair. Uncle Fester experiments with his chemistry set to produce a concoction that grows hair and tries the remedy on Itt.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Wednesday and Pugsley return in tears from trick-or-treating because a neighbor has told them there is no such thing as a witch. Morticia and Gomez plan to prove to the children that they do exist--by summoning a witch to a séance.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Determined to correct the dreadful literature that Wednesday and Pugsley are exposed to, Morticia sets out to create a new literary world. Gomez fears that his wife's first manuscript is so good, that once the publisher reads it he will lose her.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: In need of artistic fulfillment, Morticia takes up sculpting. An art critic views her first endeavor--a three-eyed Gomez statue--and clubs it with his cane. Gomez, who won't have Morticia's heart broken gets a seedy art dealer to buy it.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Pugsley copies one of his dad's old love letters and sends it to his teacher. Miss Dunbar comes to visit the Addams home and confesses to Gomez that no man has ever fallen so in love with her, leading Morticia to pretend to be the jealous wife.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: After Wednesday befriends a new boy her age, Robespierre Courtney, Morticia invites his parents, Mr. and Mrs. Henry Courtney to visit the Addams house for tea. Unbeknownst to them, the Courtney's are hoping to meet a number of the social set.

programme.title: The Addams Family
